architectural_implications.before: Embed the repository, store vectors, and answer queries with top-k similarity retrieval.

architectural_implications.before: Instrumentation inside a single process captures the full call tree automatically via in-process context.
architectural_implications.consequence: Agent runtimes need a standard convention for out-of-band context propagation, and orphaned spans become a first-class reliability/instrumentation bug class rather than an edge case.
architectural_implications.observation: Trace context must be propagated explicitly across process boundaries.

evidence_quotes.text: Agentic search gives LLMs access to CLI tools like grep, find, cat to explore code like a human.
Agentic search achieved higher accuracy with significantly fewer tokens and lower cost on TypeScript/Go test bugs.

core_insights.generalization: For domains where correctness depends on following explicit links between artifacts (imports, references, call chains), traversal-based agentic search may beat similarity-based retrieval on cost-adjusted accuracy.
core_insights.insight: On coding-agent bug-fixing tasks, agentic search (LLM driving CLI tools like grep/find/cat) outperformed vector search on accuracy while consuming significantly fewer tokens and lower cost — a single case study that inverts the default 'embed the repo and retrieve top-k chunks' retrieval architecture for code.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Retrieval for code is often assumed to be a vector-DB problem; if tool-driven exploration dominates on real repos, the retrieval layer, cost model, and latency profile of coding agents all change, and embeddings become an optimization rather than the foundation.

evidence_quotes.text: Vector search made 26 search calls on a Swe-bench run without finding the bug.
Vector search provides proximity to code but lacks connective tissue to follow import chains.

core_insights.generalization: Similarity search is a proximity primitive; any task requiring multi-hop structural traversal (dependency graphs, configs, schemas, incident timelines) needs a traversal or agentic layer on top.
core_insights.insight: The failure mode of vector search on code is not ranking quality but missing connective tissue: embeddings return text near the query but cannot follow import chains, so the agent burns many retrieval calls without ever reaching the defective code.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes the retrieval trade-off as proximity vs. connectivity, which predicts when RAG-style retrieval will fail on structured artifacts even with perfect embeddings.

evidence_quotes.text: Claude Code runs as a subprocess, resulting in missing visibility into tool calls without proper environment variable configuration.
Passing parent span IDs ensures full observability into every tool call during debugging.

core_insights.generalization: Any agent runtime that shells out to CLIs, sandboxes, or sub-agents must treat trace context as an explicit out-of-band artifact (env vars, headers, sidecar) rather than assuming in-process instrumentation.
core_insights.insight: Tracing breaks at process boundaries: when an agent runs as a subprocess (e.g., Claude Code), child-process tool calls produce orphaned spans unless the parent span ID is explicitly propagated via environment variables.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Observability is the substrate evals and debugging depend on; without cross-process context propagation, an entire class of tool calls is invisible and failures are undiagnosable.

evidence_quotes.text: A loop connecting application production logs, sampled datasets, task configurations, and scoring mechanisms.
An eval consists of a dataset, task, scoring system, and experiments.

core_insights.generalization: Reliable agent systems need the eval harness wired to production traffic, not maintained as a separate offline benchmark that drifts from real usage.
core_insights.insight: The eval framework is a closed loop that starts from production logs: logs are sampled into datasets, run through task configurations, scored, and fed back as experiments — making eval infrastructure a continuous consumer of runtime telemetry rather than a static test suite.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It places dataset curation, scoring, and experiment tracking inside the production feedback path, which dictates where logging, sampling, and scoring services must live in the system.

evidence_quotes.text: Track costs, token counts, and accuracy concurrently during experiments.
Agentic search achieved higher accuracy with significantly fewer tokens and lower cost on TypeScript/Go test bugs.

core_insights.generalization: Any agent design decision should be evaluated on a multi-objective frontier (quality, tokens, cost, latency) rather than a single accuracy number.
core_insights.insight: Experiments must be scored on accuracy, token count, and cost concurrently, because a configuration can win on quality while being economically unviable — quality metrics alone mislead architecture decisions.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Cost and latency are first-class eval dimensions for agents; treating them as afterthoughts lets expensive configurations ship and makes retrieval-architecture comparisons invalid.

evidence_quotes.text: OpenAI had to revert a model update in April 2024 because the model became too sycophantic.

core_insights.generalization: Optimizing any single model behavior creates measurable, often surprising regressions elsewhere; the mitigation is a fixed regression suite that gates every model or prompt change.
core_insights.insight: Behavioral over-optimization is a real regression class: OpenAI had to revert a model update in April 2024 because the model became too sycophantic, showing that optimizing a proxy trait (helpfulness) produces unwanted side effects that only evals catch.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Jessica Wang
  • Channel: AAIF Live
  • Main topic: Evaluating LLM coding agents using evals instead of relying on vibes
  • Purpose: To educate developers on how to design, implement, and run quantitative evaluations for AI coding agents to ensure reliable software releases. Jessica Wang from Braintrust discusses the importance of building rigorous evaluations (evals) for AI-driven coding agents rather than shipping features based on product management 'vibes'. She outlines the core components of evals—datasets, tasks, scoring, and experiments—and compares agentic search vs vector search through a real case study.

Topic Map

The Problem with Shipping on Vibes

  • Explanation: Teams often ship AI features based on anecdotal prompts working or engineering intuition, which lacks quantitative backing.
  • Key claims:
    • Shipping AI features based on vibes is problematic.
    • Engineering teams and PMs testing a couple of prompts is insufficient.
    • You need to quantify your shipping decisions.
  • Examples:
    • PMs testing a few prompts and saying it looks good.
  • Terminology:
    • vibes
    • evals
    • observability
  • Why it matters: Quantifiable evals prevent regressions in model behavior when updates are deployed.

Four Components of an Eval

  • Explanation: Creating an eval requires a dataset, a task, a scoring system, and experiment runs.
  • Key claims:
    • An eval consists of a dataset, task, scoring system, and experiments.
    • Datasets contain golden test cases, edge cases, and failure modes.
    • Scoring determines whether the model output is good or bad.
  • Examples:
    • Deterministic scoring, LLM-as-a-judge, and human review.
  • Terminology:
    • dataset
    • task
    • scoring
    • experiment
    • LLM-as-a-judge
  • Why it matters: A systematic framework is necessary to compare different configurations and prompts reliably.

Agentic Search vs. Vector Search Case Study

  • Explanation: Comparing vector search and agentic search performance on coding agent tasks using Braintrust.
  • Key claims:
    • Vector search converts text/code into numerical embeddings stored in a vector DB.
    • Agentic search gives LLMs access to CLI tools like grep, find, cat to explore code like a human.
    • Agentic search achieved higher accuracy with significantly fewer tokens and lower cost on TypeScript/Go test bugs.
  • Examples:
    • Microsoft's typescript-go repository merge PRs with 'fix' in the title.
    • Swe-bench verified Django related bug dataset.
  • Terminology:
    • vector search
    • agentic search
    • embeddings
    • Swe-bench
    • tracing
  • Why it matters: Helps engineering teams make data-driven decisions on architectural patterns for retrieval in coding assistants.

Key Points

Evals are a team sport

  • Explanation: Building effective evals requires collaboration across AI engineers, product managers, subject matter experts, and data analysts.
  • Evidence: Different roles handle dataset creation, hypothesis testing, data labeling, and scoring definitions.
  • Practical implication: Cross-functional involvement ensures comprehensive test coverage and domain-specific accuracy.

Tracing is critical for sub-processes

  • Explanation: When child processes or sub-agents run, their traces can become orphaned if parent span IDs are not passed via environment variables.
  • Evidence: Claude Code runs as a subprocess, resulting in missing visibility into tool calls without proper environment variable configuration.
  • Practical implication: Passing parent span IDs ensures full observability into every tool call during debugging.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Braintrust Evals Framework

  • How it works: A loop connecting application production logs, sampled datasets, task configurations, and scoring mechanisms.
  • Components:
    • Dataset
    • Task (Prompt & Model)
    • Scoring System
    • Experiments & Loop
  • When to use: When developing, monitoring, and iterating on LLM applications and coding agents.

Examples & Case Studies

OpenAI had to revert a model update in April 2024 because the model became too sycophantic.

  • Illustrates: Over-training models to be helpful can lead to unwanted behavioral side effects.
  • Lesson: Evals help catch nuances and over-optimization early in model updates.

Vector search made 26 search calls on a Swe-bench run without finding the bug.

  • Illustrates: Vector search provides proximity to code but lacks connective tissue to follow import chains.
  • Lesson: Agentic search follows code logic like a human, leading to better results with fewer tokens.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Stop relying on vibes; define test datasets and scoring criteria before shipping AI features.
    • Pass parent span IDs as environment variables when tracing subprocesses.
    • Use loop queries to analyze experiment results and identify failure patterns.
  • Strategic:
    • Agentic search outperforms basic vector search on complex codebases by enabling multi-step exploration.
    • Evals require cross-functional collaboration between engineers, PMs, and subject matter experts.
    • Track costs, token counts, and accuracy concurrently during experiments.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How can hybrid search approaches combine vector search and agentic search effectively?
    • How do we prevent LLM-based evaluation tools from artificially inflating token counts or introducing bias?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Agentic search is more cost-efficient and accurate than basic vector search on codebases. (empirical)
  • OpenAI reverted a model update in April 2024 because ChatGPT became too sycophantic. (historical)

Notable Quotes

"Evals ensure that you're not playing whack-a-mole when developing your AI products." "Evals are a team sport."

Compressed Summary

  • Evals consist of datasets, tasks, scoring, and experiments.
  • Agentic search enables LLMs to navigate code via CLI tools like grep and find.
  • Proper tracing requires passing parent span IDs to subprocesses.
  • Vector search returns code chunks but lacks connective reasoning compared to agentic search.
  • Keywords: evals, coding agents, vector search, agentic search, observability
  • Core insight: Building rigorous quantitative evaluations prevents teams from shipping AI features based on vibes and reveals that agentic search outperforms vector search in code reasoning tasks.
